Fix a review finding in michi's NAPI byte accounting. Repo orin-dx/michi. Work on the existing branch `refactor/one-render-path` (PR #141): `git fetch origin refactor/one-render-path` and check it out (create a local branch tracking it; its head is 58363219 or later). Read AGENTS.md and PRINCIPLES.md (prefix shell commands with `rtk`; `cargo nextest run`; no unwrap/expect in lib; comments plain, wrapped at 120 cols; every claim needs a test that fails when broken — prove with a mutant and revert). Commit (`fix(napi): ...`, no session links or Claude-Session trailers) and push to `refactor/one-render-path` (normal push; never force; never main). Do not open PRs. `just check`/`just test` must run outside the sandbox (moon locks .git/config).

## The finding (Medium, crates/michi-core/src/napi/outcome.rs:147)
"Removing `renderPipeline` leaves no way to render some previously valid reports: 10,000 pending steps with five-byte IDs and 1,660-byte ASCII names pass the 16 MiB input check (`napi/input.rs:394–405`, `napi/response.rs:478–484`), but row and truncation bookkeeping push even a fresh builder over the cumulative cap (`response.rs:232–240, 304–310`). The replacement throws instead of returning a table with truncated cells; the same cumulative check affects the partial-success and status replacements (`response.rs:297–324`). Preserve the former single-report input capacity while keeping a separate bound on retained data and rendered output."

Context: PR #141 removed the standalone JS renderers (renderPipeline, renderPartialSuccess, renderStatus, renderAlreadyDone, renderDomainError) so AgentResponse is the one path. `JsAgentResponse` holds a cumulative `held` total (strings plus structural charges: ROW_OVERHEAD/OUTCOME_ROW memory per row, SECTION_OVERHEAD, ERROR_OVERHEAD, HINT_OVERHEAD, `cost::table_repeats` for names a `truncated`/`totalCount` table writes again) capped at `input::MAX_INPUT_BYTES` (16 MiB). The documented guarantee (response.rs ~:138, napi/cost.rs header, napi/input.rs) is that a render is at most 19x the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface (text, JSON, toCallToolResult) and stays under V8's string limit; `crates/michi-core/src/napi/response/output_bound.rs` measures it over a matrix of hostile responses. A sibling fix already landed (58363219): error causes are charged text+HINT_OVERHEAD instead of text+String overhead.

## Required outcome (all must hold)
1. Every single call that passes its own per-call checks succeeds on a fresh `AgentResponse` (items, kvItems, partialSuccess, pipeline, status, alreadyDone, error, and the hint/recovery/humanContent setters), including the finding's case (10,000 pending steps, 5-byte ids, 1,660-byte names) and the equivalent worst cases for partialSuccess and status. Add tests for each that fail on today's code.
2. Retained memory stays bounded: many calls cannot accumulate unbounded rows/cells (keep the protection ROW_OVERHEAD exists for, e.g. repeated `items(Array(100000).fill([]), ...)`).
3. Rendered output stays bounded and under V8's max string length on every surface; restate the guarantee precisely in the docs (response.rs AgentResponse doc, cost.rs header, input.rs constants) and keep `output_bound.rs` proving it (extend the matrix with the new worst cases, including maximal structure + maximal strings together).
4. No response accepted today is rejected afterwards (don't make any limit stricter).
The finding's suggested shape: keep strings capped at 16 MiB cumulative (so one call's worth of strings always fits) and count structural/bookkeeping charges against a separate cap sized so that 19x(strings) + (structure's real output multiplier)x(structure) + 4 KiB stays under V8's limit. Derive the structure cap and its multiplier from the writers, not by guessing; if a single combined cap with headroom is cleaner and provably meets 1-4, that's acceptable — explain the choice. Error messages for the new cap must name it clearly (e.g. `cumulative structure total N exceeds maximum of M`); keep the existing `cumulative byte total` message for strings.

## Docs/changeset
Update packages/michi-node/README.md and docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md where the limits are described. Add one bullet to `.changeset/js-one-render-path.md` (user-first, JS terms) only if the visible limit behaviour changes for JS users (e.g. "any report a single call accepts now fits a new `AgentResponse`"); do not edit other changesets.

## Verify (exit codes)
`just check`, `just test` (scaling tests are wall-clock and flake under load; if only `michi-core::scaling` fails, rerun it alone and report `uptime`), the output-bound tests, and a mutant per new guarantee (e.g. charge structure against the string cap again → the finding's test fails; drop the structure cap → a retained-memory test fails).

## Report
Commit SHA; the design (caps, constants, how the output bound is derived and its new formula); tests added and their mutants; check exit codes; anything that couldn't be met. Under ~700 words.

# Principles

Two questions come up over and over: **should this go in michi?** and **how should this work get done?** This doc answers both, so nobody — human or agent — has to re-derive the reasoning from scratch each time. It's the "why" behind `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not a replacement for either.

---

## What belongs in michi

A primitive earns a place here only if it clears all five gates below. These are yes/no checks with evidence, not vibes — if you can't point to the evidence, it doesn't clear the gate yet.

### 1. Rendering, not domain logic

It turns already-decided data into agent-readable strings/types. It doesn't decide _what_ data survives.

- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
- Rendering makes output syntactically safe, not trustworthy: it keeps one value from creating extra lines, fields or cells, and it does not judge what a value says. See the [trust model](docs/spec/02-toon-format.md#trust-model).
- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.

### 2. Small default dependency set

The default build depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`. Anything else is opt-in behind a Cargo feature.

- Adding a mandatory dependency needs a recorded decision in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`. Prefer caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait) first.

### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed

Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.

- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.
- A pattern seen in only one tool — however heavily repeated inside that tool — isn't there yet. Watch for a second independent confirmation before building it.

### 4. Doesn't duplicate an existing primitive

Check `hints` / `recovery` / `idempotency` / `status` / `error` / `mcp` first. Verify the distinction concretely — don't assume novelty from a vibe.

- "This looks similar to X" means go read X's source, not assume it's covered.
- Example: a proposed "diagnostics" primitive looked adjacent to `idempotency::PartialSuccess` — until actually reading `PartialSuccess`'s doc comment showed it's scoped to multi-step _mutating_ operations, not read-path degradation. They turned out genuinely distinct, but that took checking, not assuming either way.

### 5. Deviations get tracked, not silently absorbed

Where the final shape diverges from the original ask or an earlier draft, it goes in a Design Decisions table. Spec and code should never quietly drift apart.

---

## Split the decision from the signal

Gate 1's ceiling ("stay generic" vs. "real tools need real sophistication") isn't a tension to compromise on — it's usually an architecture problem. Separate the _domain-specific decision_ from the _universal signal_.

**Worked example: truncation.** Deciding _which_ items survive a budget is tool-specific — personalized-PageRank over a call graph, a statistical outlier-preserving sampler, a simple first-N cutoff. None of that belongs in michi. But _reporting_ what got cut, in a consistent agent-readable shape, is exactly what every tool needs regardless of how it decided.

**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to render an error, a batch's outcomes, pipeline state, a status report or an already-done report. The standalone functions that duplicated it are removed. Below, `r` is `new AgentResponse(name)`.

- `renderDomainError(code, message, hints, false, causes)` → `r.error(code, message, causes)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderDomainError(code, message, [], true)` → `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)`.
- `renderPartialSuccess(completed, failed, skipped)` → `r.partialSuccess('partial_success', completed, failed, skipped)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderPipeline(steps)` → `r.pipeline('step', steps)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderStatus(toolName, description, items, hints)` → `r.status(toolName, description, items)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderAlreadyDone(operation, summary, hints)` → `r.alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `alreadyDone(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` type are removed: check your stored result yourself (`stored != null`).

The replacements also give you `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()`. Like any response, they cut a table cell over 200 characters and list it in the `truncated` block; the removed functions never cut.

# michi

TypeScript/JavaScript bindings for [`michi`](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) — AXI response primitives for agent-ergonomic tools. Native binary via NAPI-RS: no WASM, no JS reimplementation of the rendering logic.

## Install

```bash
npm i @orin-dx/michi
```

npm installs the matching prebuilt binary as an optional dependency; see [Supported platforms](#supported-platforms).

## Quick start

```typescript
import { AgentResponse } from "@orin-dx/michi";

const response = new AgentResponse("issues");
response.items(
  [
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51815 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "[Bug]: Telegram plugin" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51812 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "dark mode request" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
  ],
  ["number", "title", "state"],
  8771,
);
response.hint("Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue");

process.stdout.write(response.renderText());
```

```text
issues[2]{number,title,state}:
  51815,"[Bug]: Telegram plugin",open
  51812,dark mode request,open
totalCount: 8771
help[1]: Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue
```

## API

Every string these functions return for an agent is a TOON 4.4 document with no trailing newline — lists, key-value blocks, errors, status, recovery hints and help blocks alike. The one exception is `renderGithubAnnotation`, which writes for GitHub Actions, not for an agent.

### Free functions

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `renderToon` | `(opts: ToonOptions) => string` — one TOON list (`typeName`, `fields`, `rows`): the entry and a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block for any cut cell. `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to `AgentResponse` |
| `renderHints` | `(hints: string[]) => string` — the inline array `help[N]: h1,h2` |
| `appendHints` | `(body: string, hints: string[]) => string` — append `help[N]: …` to a document, on its own line |
| `renderRecovery` | `(hints: RecoveryHint[]) => string` — the table `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` (`params` is `"{}"` here; an absent reason is `null`) |
| `renderKv` | `(items: KvItem[]) => string` — `key: value` lines; throws `kv_validation_failed: …` for a repeated key or a reserved key (a root key michi writes, such as `help` or `message`) |
| `renderGithubAnnotation` | `(code, message) => string` — a GitHub Actions annotation, `::error title={code}::{message}`, on one line (`%`, CR and LF in the message are encoded). For the error an agent reads, use `AgentResponse.error()` |
| `truncate` | `(content: string, maxChars: number) => { content, originalChars, removed, wasTruncated }` — text that fits comes back unchanged; a longer text keeps its first `maxChars - 1` chars and ends in `…`, and the cut is reported in `removed` and `wasTruncated`, never inside `content`. Add your own hint, for example `cut ${removed} of ${originalChars} chars; pass full=true`, to the response's `help[]`. |
| `parseRetryAfter` | `(headerValue: string) => number \| null` — an RFC 9110 `Retry-After` value (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) in seconds; a past date is `0`, a malformed value `null` |
| `nextRetryDelay` | `(maxRetries, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitterFactor, jitterSeed, attempt, retryAfterMs?) => number \| null` — the next back-off delay in ms, or `null` once retries are used up; pass a random `jitterSeed` in `[0, 1]` per call |
| `isRetryableStatus` | `(status: number) => boolean` — `true` for 429, 502, 503 and 504; retry 502 and 504 only for idempotent requests |

### `AgentResponse` class

The primary integration point — a builder that composes TOON/KV rendering, hints, and recovery into one response. Errors, batch outcomes, pipeline state, status and already-done reports are parts of it too, so a batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is one document, one JSON object and one MCP result.

Setters return `void`, not `this`, so call them as sequential statements rather than a chain. (Chaining isn't supported across the NAPI boundary — see `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md` in the main repo for why.)

| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `(typeName: string)` |
| `.items` | `(rows: ToonValue[][], fields: string[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a TOON list section named for the response's type; each call adds one, rendered in call order. `totalCount` is how many rows existed before a cut and renders only when it is larger than the rows passed |
| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full. Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.error` | `(code, message, causes?, retryable?) => void` — report a classified error: it renders first (`error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`), `isError` is true everywhere, and the JSON carries `error: {code, message, causes, retryable}` beside `hints` and `recovery`. One per response |
| `.partialSuccess` | `(name, completed: CompletedOp[], failed: FailedOp[], skipped: SkippedOp[]) => void` (throws when an `index` repeats) — append a batch's outcomes as the list `name[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, a row per op sorted by `index` (the op's position in your batch; `status` is `completed`, `failed` or `skipped`; `reason` is the failure reason, the skip token or `null`); failed ops' recovery hints join the one `recovery` table |
| `.pipeline` | `(name, steps: PipelineStep[]) => void` — append `name[N]{id,name,status,reason}:`; `status` is a `StepStatus` label (`completed`, `outcome_unknown`, …) and `reason` is required exactly for `outcome_unknown`, `skipped` and `not_run` |
| `.status` | `(toolName, description, items: StatusItem[]) => void` — append `tool`, `description` and `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:`; add hints with `.hint` |
| `.alreadyDone` | `(operation, summary) => void` — append `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary`, for an operation your idempotency check found already done |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"error":{...},"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` (`error` and `sections` only when set) |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

## Input and output limits

Every export that takes arrays or strings rejects oversize input with a thrown `Error` before it does any work (for example `rows length 100001 exceeds maximum of 100000`). The caps:

- 100,000 rows; 1,000 fields, values per row, KV items or status items; 10,000 hints, causes, steps or partial-success entries; 1,000,000 cells per call.
- 1 MiB per cell value, hint, reason, message or step name; 4 KiB per type name, field name, key, tool or identifier.
- **16 MiB of string data** per call, and per `AgentResponse` across all its calls (`input byte total … exceeds maximum of 16777216`, `cumulative byte total … exceeds maximum of 16777216`). This was 64 MiB before it was found to bound only the input: a render writes up to 19 times the bytes it holds (control characters are the worst case), so 64 MiB could produce 1.2 GiB and a `renderJson()` string over V8's limit. At 16 MiB every render stays under 304 MiB, so a response either renders in every format or is rejected up front.

## Supported platforms

Prebuilt native binaries ship for:

- macOS on Apple silicon (`darwin-arm64`, package `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-arm64`)
- macOS on Intel (`darwin-x64`, package `@orin-dx/michi-darwin-x64`)
- Linux x64 with glibc (`linux-x64-gnu`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-x64-gnu`)
- Linux x64 with musl (`linux-x64-musl`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-x64-musl`)
- Linux arm64 with glibc (`linux-arm64-gnu`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-arm64-gnu`)
- Linux arm64 with musl (`linux-arm64-musl`, package `@orin-dx/michi-linux-arm64-musl`)

Windows isn't supported yet. Building from source needs a Rust toolchain (see [`rust-toolchain.toml`](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/blob/main/rust-toolchain.toml) in the main repo).

**Breaking:** `AgentResponse` is now the one way to render an error, a batch's outcomes, pipeline state, a status report or an already-done report. The standalone functions that duplicated it are removed. Below, `r` is `new AgentResponse(name)`.

- `renderDomainError(code, message, hints, false, causes)` → `r.error(code, message, causes)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderDomainError(code, message, [], true)` → `renderGithubAnnotation(code, message)`.
- `renderPartialSuccess(completed, failed, skipped)` → `r.partialSuccess('partial_success', completed, failed, skipped)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderPipeline(steps)` → `r.pipeline('step', steps)`, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderStatus(toolName, description, items, hints)` → `r.status(toolName, description, items)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `renderAlreadyDone(operation, summary, hints)` → `r.alreadyDone(operation, summary)`, a `r.hint(h)` per hint, then `r.renderText()`.
- `alreadyDone(stored)` and the `AlreadyDone` type are removed: check your stored result yourself (`stored != null`).

The fix is pushed to `refactor/one-render-path` as **d33ac7c7** (`fix(napi): cap an AgentResponse's strings and structure separately`), a normal push on top of 58363219. No PR was opened. Requirements 2–4 hold; requirement 1 holds for every call the tests cover, but not for every possible call (see the last section).

A local branch `refactor/one-render-path` was already checked out, stale, in another worktree (`agent-a55981bc7678af679`). So I committed on a local branch `fix/napi-structure-cap` and pushed it with `HEAD:refactor/one-render-path`.

## Design: two cumulative caps, the second on the sum
- **Strings, 16 MiB** (`MAX_INPUT_BYTES`). This counts only caller strings. It equals the per-call string cap, so one call's strings always fit a fresh builder. The type name now counts as structure, so a 4 KiB name no longer eats into that room. The error message is unchanged: `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216`.
- **Held, 26 MiB** (new `MAX_HELD_BYTES`), meaning strings plus structure. Structure is row, cell and String storage, section and error overheads, the hint/cause/recovery allowances, the type name, and the repeats from `table_repeats` and `fixed_table_repeats`. The new message is `cumulative held total N exceeds maximum of 27262976`.
- Every charge is the same number of bytes as before; I only sorted each into strings or structure, with a `Charge {strings, structure}` per slot. So the measured 19x factor still applies to the held total.
- **New bound:** a render is at most 19 × held + 4 KiB, which is at most 19 × 26 MiB + 4 KiB = 494 MiB on every surface. That stays under V8's limit of 2^29 − 24, checked by a compile-time assert. 26 is the largest whole MiB that does (27 would be 513 MiB).

**Why one cap on the sum rather than a separate structure cap:** before this change, responses holding up to 16 MiB of pure structure were accepted (e.g. six `items(Array(100000).fill([]))` calls). Keeping them (requirement 4) means a structure cap of at least 16 MiB. At 19x for both strings and structure that totals 608 MiB, over V8's limit. Structure does need the full 19x: the allowances were sized for it, and KV floats reach about 19x on their storage charge. A cap on the sum meets requirements 2–4 and reuses the existing proof.

## Tests (all in `output_bound.rs`)
- **Fit tests**, each one call at its caps on a fresh builder with a 4 KiB type name. Each asserts its per-call string charge is within 64 KiB of 16 MiB without passing it:
  - the finding's pipeline case
  - a pipeline with every cell cut
  - partialSuccess with 30,000 cut entries plus recovery hints
  - status, kvItems, items, a million cells, and an error with a 1 MiB message
  - alreadyDone and every setter
- **Render tests** for the same cases using `\u{1}`, the worst escape, checking both the bound and V8's limit.
- **`both_caps_at_once_render_within_the_bound`:** about 16 MiB of strings and over 9 MiB of structure together.
- I strengthened the retained-rows test to require the held-cap message, and updated the tests whose counts changed. In the Node suite, 16 one-MiB hints now fit, the long-name tables accept about 6,200 rows or steps (I checked the 6,272-row figure in Node), and I added a Node test for the finding's case.

## Mutants (each reverted)
- **Strings plus structure checked against the 16 MiB string cap (the old behaviour):** 20 tests fail, including every fit test except the setters and alreadyDone, which already fit before.
- **Held cap removed:** the retained-rows test, the empty-sections test and the review's 60,000-row reproduction test fail.
- **Type name charged as a string:** the full-items tests and the hint-cap test fail.

## Checks
- `just check`: exit 0.
- `just test`: exit 0. Rust 1235/1235; Node 184/184, confirmed in a log file of my own because the shared tmp log was being overwritten by another session. The scaling tests did not flake.
- napi and output-bound tests run directly: 139/139 pass. The slowest output-bound test takes about 10 s in debug.

## Docs
I updated the `AgentResponse` doc, the `cost.rs` header, the `input.rs` constants, the `napi.rs` module doc and pinned-constants test, `packages/michi-node/README.md` and `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md`. I added one user-facing bullet to `.changeset/js-one-render-path.md`. I removed `value::cell_cost`, which had no remaining users. I did not touch `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`; its 16 MiB entry is now partly out of date, if you want a decision line there.

## What couldn't be met
Requirement 1 can't hold for every call with the current per-call checks:
- **Calls with long names and many cut cells.** The names written again for each cut cell are not limited per call. A pipeline with a 4 KiB section name and 20,000 cut cells charges 82 MB of repeats, and its render can't fit under V8's limit at all. These calls stay rejected, as they were before.
- **Where it is guaranteed.** A partialSuccess or pipeline at its caps fits with a section name up to about 100 bytes (tested). An items call fits while its strings plus 24 bytes per row and cell stay within 26 MiB, so a million cells can't also carry 16 MiB of strings.
- **What would lift the items limit.** Giving cell storage its own lower multiplier, which needs a further split of structure. I didn't attempt it.
